clue.text: A group on leave

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group, of musicians for instance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whole team or band is away on holiday at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a noun (time off work) in the surface, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a place or person is to desert it, a stronger synonym for the verb leave.

clue.text: A child that is initially very eager to win

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for child
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A child who is very keen to win at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to attain or gain it, a synonym of the verb win as in win a prize.

clue.text: Idiot in charge of the RAF?

blocks.note: first meaning: a silly, empty-headed person
second meaning, read as two words: the head of the air force

explanation.surface: A jibe that a fool is running Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a playful split into AIR plus HEAD; the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is informal for a stupid person, as if their head held only air.

clue.text: Remained blue over ending of employment

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, so the word is read upwards
the ending of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: blue can mean smutty or indecent, as in blue jokes
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone stayed on feeling sad after their job came to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like sad, but here it means risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to live or stay in a place, so it means remained.

clue.text: Bad reputation for opposition to disturbance announced by Yemeni leader

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the phrase is taken by its sound
the leader of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: saying no to a riot, said quickly
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A Yemeni leader announces opposition to unrest and gains a bad name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, so it is an ill reputation or infamy.

clue.text: Cried during infected pus being cleaned

indicators.note: something infected has been corrupted, so the letters are spoilt into a new order
one thing happening during another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to cry is to weep; the past tense
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed while a wound full of infected pus was being cleaned out.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are split around the crying word: S before it, UP after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swept up is a phrasal verb for tidied away with a brush, so a floor swept up has been cleaned.

clue.text: Cut out delay

blocks.note: first meaning: of an engine, to stop running
second meaning: to play for time

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a hold-up from a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that stalls stops abruptly, and to stall for time is to use delaying tactics.

clue.text: Urge limits to exaggeration about how old we are

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, so the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
C is short for circa, about
our age states how old we are

explanation.surface: A warning against exaggerating our ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container instruction, but it is C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is to urge them on, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Wave in Thailand capsized one man beside you and me

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the words are read upwards

blocks.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A man capsized by a giant wave off Thailand, recalling the 2004 disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake, so it is a kind of wave.

clue.text: Order to touch bird gently

blocks.note: to pat is to touch lightly, the sense the clue's last word adds
a tern is a seabird
gives no letters: it qualifies the touch, making it a light tap

explanation.surface: An instruction to stroke a bird softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gently' sits at the end but qualifies 'touch': to touch gently is to pat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is an orderly arrangement or regular design, so it means order in that sense.

clue.text: Gather in front section of harlequin garment

indicators.note: the front section of a word is its opening few letters, so only the start is kept

blocks.note: the first three letters of the clown's name
a vest is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: Collect up the front part of a harlequin's colourful costume.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest crops is to gather them in from the fields, so the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Report of a hundred in number

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a count is a number, as in the total of a tally

explanation.surface: A news report of about a hundred people being involved.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative report or description of events, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Opt for spoken language test for those entitled to vote

blocks.note: to elect is to choose or opt for
an oral is a spoken examination, often in a foreign language

explanation.surface: Choosing a spoken language exam as a qualification for voters.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'for' belongs to the wordplay phrase, the second starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral describes things belonging to electors, the citizens who have the right to vote, such as the electoral roll.

clue.text: Employment in America takes a long time

blocks.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America
an age is a very long period, as in 'it took an age'

explanation.surface: Getting a job in America is a slow process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employment' looks like a job, but it is in the sense of putting something to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used, and employment of a tool or word means its use.

clue.text: Some men do well to provide financial support

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are wanted, a run lying across them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Certain men are successful enough to be able to back things with money.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow a college or prize is to give it a permanent income, a form of funding.

clue.text: It's of no use to throw out a smaller quantity

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: There's no point discarding a smaller amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' reads as one phrasal verb, discard, but the second word only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless has no value or utility, so it is useless.

clue.text: Due to ANC, I abandoned schooling

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters are let loose into a new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A South African speaking of leaving school because of the African National Congress, the ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling and education both mean the instruction given to children in school.

clue.text: Dundee CID could be in two minds

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: Detectives in Dundee, a Scottish city, can't make up their minds; CID is the police Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in two minds is an idiom for being unsure which way to choose, the state of being irresolute.

clue.text: Sacked second ancient city captured in heroic exploit

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so these pieces go within the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad
a deed is a feat or exploit, as in deeds of valour

explanation.surface: Troy was sacked, a heroic feat recounted in legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' looks like dismissed from a job, but here it means plundered, fitting the Trojan surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacked city has been plundered and laid waste, that is, ruined or wrecked.

clue.text: Downgraded duke let his feelings show

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
to emote is to display emotion openly

explanation.surface: A nobleman broke down in emotion after losing rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To be demoted is to be reduced to a lower rank or position.

clue.text: Surfboarder's opening advantage is more than needed

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its start, so only its first letters are kept

blocks.note: the first three letters of this word
a plus is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A surfer's head start gives an edge beyond what is required.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening here takes three letters, not the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an excess, an amount left over beyond what is required.

clue.text: Die in agony by court order

indicators.note: someone in agony writhes and twists, so the letters are contorted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone sentenced to a painful death by order of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court order' reads as a single legal phrase, but 'court' belongs to the wordplay and 'order' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command issued by authority, so a synonym of the noun order.

clue.text: I will say nearly everything wrong

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
e.g. means for example, that is, say
all is everything

explanation.surface: Someone admitting that nearly everything they say will be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the verb of speaking, but it stands for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means against the law, so it is wrong in the sense of unlawful.

clue.text: Old soldiers voluntarily left in the centre of London without specific agreement

indicators.note: one thing left in another sits within it, so this piece goes inside the next

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force, since renamed
L is the abbreviation for left
the City is London's historic centre and financial district

explanation.surface: Veterans who volunteered stayed on in central London without any formal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The centre of London' looks like a letter-selection instruction for its middle letter, but it is the City itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitly means in an implied or unspoken way, so something agreed tacitly has no explicit agreement.

clue.text: Demonstration starting from Marble Arch

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest begins at Marble Arch, a London landmark where marches often start.
explanation.walkthrough: The landmark's name nearly hides the answer, but its letters run M-A-R-B, so the first word gives only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a protest walk by demonstrators, so it is one kind of demonstration.

clue.text: Ice mostly goes with drink containing gin, say

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: alcohol is strong drink
taken as written, before shortening

explanation.surface: A cocktail where most of the ice is served alongside a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: gin is given as an example of an alcoholic spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink with spirits such as gin in it contains alcohol, which is what alcoholic describes.

clue.text: Bill and Edward played their part

blocks.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Edward each did their share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name to pair with Edward, but it is an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform a role on stage, so acted means played a part.

clue.text: That man's holding a record for domestics

indicators.note: something holding another has it within, so the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: he's is the contraction of he is
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man clutching a vinyl album for the household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Helps, as a plural noun, is an old word for domestic servants.
explanation.definitionFit: A help is a domestic servant or cleaner, so helps are domestics, the household employees.

clue.text: Most difficult of everything in the exam

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits within it, so the first piece is set inside the second

blocks.note: all means everything
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Picking out the hardest question of all on the exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tall order' is a hard task, so tall can mean difficult and the superlative means most difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall in the idiom a tall order means demanding, so the superlative is the most demanding or hardest.

clue.text: Please remove the illuminations!

blocks.note: first meaning: to give great pleasure to
second meaning, read as DE- plus LIGHT: to take the lights away

explanation.surface: A polite request to turn off the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite word attached to the order, but it is a verb in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to charm or please them greatly; split as de-light it humorously means to strip of lights.

clue.text: Detective almost half suspects journalist is no longer working

indicators.note: almost half is a little under half the word, so only its first three letters are kept

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
taken as written, before shortening
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A detective with half his suspects in hand and a reporter who has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of the eight-letter word would be four letters; almost half is three.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused has gone out of use, so it is idle and no longer operating.

clue.text: Exhibition to show contempt for freedom of movement

blocks.note: to dis someone is slang for showing them disrespect
play is slack or room to move, as in play in a rope

explanation.surface: An exhibition intended to sneer at freedom of movement, the EU right to travel and work.
explanation.definitionFit: A display is a public show or exhibition of goods or art, so the nouns are synonyms.
